tier_reason: The wiki Benchmarks page (5 revisions, all by the author on 2020-06-04) shows hyperfine output for vips.exe and criterion output for Photon, matching the record exactly, but gives no CPU, OS, compiler, Rust/libvips versions or image sizes, and the PNG bench code was never committed. First-party numbers with partial methodology, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Wiki Benchmarks page (2020-06-04, photon-rs 0.2.0): PNG invert and save, Photon criterion [238.46 ms 244.87 ms 254.62 ms] vs libvips vips.exe 915.1 ms +/- 36.0 ms (10 runs), about 3.7x faster (derived from page data). JPG invert and save, Photon [114.67 ms 117.26 ms 122.22 ms] vs libvips 84.2 ms +/- 12.0 ms (18 runs), so libvips is about 1.39x faster (derived from page data). Mixed result: one win (PNG), one loss (JPG).
corrections.caveats: Mixed result: Photon wins the PNG invert-and-save case (about 3.7x, derived from page data) but libvips wins the JPG case (about 1.39x, derived from page data). First-party wiki numbers from 2020-06-04 (photon-rs 0.2.0 at that commit), never updated; no CPU, OS, compiler, rustc or libvips version, image dimensions or encoder settings (PNG compression level, JPEG quality) are given, so the PNG gap may reflect encoder settings rather than the pixel operation. The two sides are timed differently: Photon in an in-process criterion loop (10 samples) of open, invert and save; libvips through hyperfine on the Windows vips.exe command line, which includes process start-up. Hyperfine reports only 6.2 ms user and 13.1 ms system CPU for the 915 ms PNG run, so its CPU accounting does not cover the vips work. The bench at the matching commit b802192 (crate/benches/photon_benchmark.rs, 2020-06-04) opens examples/input_images/input.jpg and saves output.jpg; no PNG variant was ever committed and the PNG test image is an imgur link, so the PNG number (the only win) cannot be reproduced from the repo. The page introduction promises ImageMagick and PIL comparisons but only libvips numbers appear. Invert is a trivial per-pixel colour op and says nothing about resampling; the current bench (crate/benches/photon_benchmark.rs) adds resize_png/resize_jpg with Lanczos3 but no published numbers against any baseline. Baseline is neither ImageMagick nor stb_image_resize.

notes: Numbers verified verbatim on the wiki page and its revision history; the record's bench path benches/photon_benchmark.rs is really crate/benches/photon_benchmark.rs, and at the wiki's date it only benchmarked a JPG. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE.md), 3.9k stars, 190 forks, not archived, not a fork, last commit 2026-09-18. Keep as a C entry with the mixed-result and category-fit shortcomings.

tier_reason: The README gives only absolute AVIR timings (245 ms single thread, 74 ms with 8 threads, i7-7700K, Intel C++ 18.2 AVX2) and an unquantified 'up to three times faster' LANCIR-vs-AVIR claim; no third-party resizer (stb_image_resize, ImageMagick, OpenCV, libvips, IPP) is timed anywhere in the repo, and the Comparison section (other/frtest.cpp) measures frequency response and dynamic range against Lanczos-3, not speed. No speed comparison against an incumbent, so D.

corrections.caveats: Tier D: the README's only speed comparison is LANCIR against the author's own AVIR ('up to three times faster', no numbers); AVIR's 245 ms / 74 ms (1 / 8 threads) downscale timing on an i7-7700K with Intel C++ 18.2 AVX2 has no baseline, and the timing harness is not in the repo. LANCIR's 'likely one of the fastest available for CPUs' names no competitor. The README's Comparison section (other/frtest.cpp, _fr_up.png, _dr_up.png) is a quality comparison (frequency response, dynamic range) against Lanczos-3, not a speed result. lancir.h contains no benchmark figures. No numeric comparison against stb_image_resize or ImageMagick exists in the repo; a web search found none from third parties either. Notability is borderline (502 stars, 49 forks), though the README lists users (MLV App, Trainz, LVC Audio, Contaware, PretextSnapshot). AVIR's focus is quality, not speed. Separate library from the author's r8brain-free-src (audio resampler); not a duplicate.

notes: Confirmed at D: repo top level (avir.h, avir_dil.h, avir_float4_sse.h, avir_float8_avx.h, lancir.h, bin/, other/) and other/ (frtest.cpp, avirdoxy.txt, three PNG plots) hold no speed comparison against any third-party resizer. Metadata checked: MIT (LICENSE and lancir.h header), 502 stars, not archived, not a fork, last commit 2026-08-22 (LANCIR 3.1.1). Below 1k stars at tier D, but keep per the keep-and-document rule.
